assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large clinical outcomes and broad physiological impact; the arc from hormone biology to drugs is clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and biology of proglucagon-derived peptides and GLP-1 action; Knudsen led development of the long-acting therapeutic analogues. Mojsov's early peptide characterization is a real credit question, and the three-person cap forces a choice among four credited names.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at large scale over many years with independent confirmation; recognition appears timely, with ongoing expansion of indications.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen and other contributors not in the list is contested.
Whether the committee prefers basic physiology or the therapeutic development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and a general principle of proteostasis, with relevance to diabetes, cancer and neurodegeneration. Conceptually original and mechanistically complete.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently dissected the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 pathway in yeast and mammals; the pairing is natural and supported by the supplied credit. Others, such as David Ron on PERK/eIF2alpha signaling, are not in the credited names, so the configuration may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed by decades of independent work; the field is mature and recognition would be timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the PERK and ATF6 branches require additional recognition outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory leukemias and lymphomas, establishing a new class of living therapeutics with large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed the costimulatory CAR designs underlying approved products; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified lymphocytes. Contributions by Eshhar, Gross and others are not in the supplied credit, so the configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent clinical confirmation; long-term follow-up is maturing, though solid tumor translation remains limited.
uncertainties: Priority among CAR conceptual inventors, costimulation designers and clinical developers is unresolved.
Toxicity and limited efficacy beyond hematological malignancies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, converting a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one and validating splicing correction as a therapeutic principle. Strong from an RNA-processing viewpoint.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target logic, with Bennett leading antisense chemistry and drug development; the pair is coherent. Other academic contributors to SMN2 targeting and the SMN1 gene discovery are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with years of real-world and trial confirmation; recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Whether SMN1 gene identification and the antisense work form a compound discovery needing separate recognition.
Contribution split between the academic and company teams.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the nutrient-responsive growth regulator that integrates metabolism, aging and cancer biology; widely influential and conceptually foundational.
assessment.attribution: Hall's yeast genetics identifying TOR is the decisive origin; Schreiber's rapamycin/FKBP12 chemical biology and Sabatini's mTOR work in mammals are real but secondary to the core discovery and Sabatini's candidacy is complicated. A sole-laureate proposal is plausible but credit with others is open.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed across species and disease contexts; mature, possibly overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the discovery as including the mammalian mTOR and chemical biology contributions.
Strength of direct clinical consequences relative to the basic mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle of intracellular organization reframed how cells compartmentalize biochemistry and has transformed cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated phase-separated P granules in C. elegans embryos, the foundational demonstration. Görlich and McKnight contributed related work on FG repeats and low-complexity domains, and four names compete for at most three places.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted but still contested in terms of physiological relevance and in vivo mechanisms; possibly premature.
uncertainties: Debate over how generally condensates are functionally causal in vivo.
Credit allocation among four candidates and early related work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition created the model of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, turning chronic myeloid leukemia into a largely manageable disease and validating oncogene addiction.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led drug discovery, Druker the clinical translation and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. Credit is conceptually clear for the three, though the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries (Rowley, Nowell, de Klein and others) are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and a changed standard of care; fully mature, although earlier cancer-gene discoveries have already been recognised.
uncertainties: Whether the translational story adds enough beyond earlier recognised oncogene work.
Allocation between drug discovery and clinical development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5 stem cells created a widely used platform for tissue biology, disease modeling and personalized medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader of the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid work; Sato performed the first organoid derivation as a lead author. Contributions from other organoid pioneers, such as pluripotent-stem-cell-based systems, are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Rapid, broad adoption with independent replication; clinical translation is still developing, so timing may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Overlap with Lgr5 stem cell discovery and pluripotent organoid approaches.
Extent of clinical impact still maturing.
